x: On June 3rd we sent a team to Morden for a 4 x 176 yds. relay, and on a rough track our team of Ron Holtum, John Benstead, Ron Morrell and Dudley Gordon ran out winners of a close race.
In the 440 yards Dudley Gordon finished 2nd; John Davis won the 880 yards with George Davidson fourth. The two miles was won by Dave Baulch with Don Stroud 2nd and Dave Hooper 3rd.

Alan Jackson and Dudley Gordon were finalists in the 400m. and a welcome entry in the 400m. hurdles was Brian Coleman. In the 3000m. walk our Olympic men Stan Vickers and Eric Hall filled 1st. and 3rd. places.

Dudley Gordon ran his best quarter ever. Not knowing who was in front of him, he just "went" and surprised us all with his determined running, handing over second to Dennis Butler for the first furlong.

The race was won by Linford (T.V.H.) for Lensbury in 2m.0.8s., on a five laps to the mile grass track. Dudley Gordon was unlucky not to win the 440, losing by inches, after leading all the way - he also doubled up in the 100yds.

Jock Cameron, making a welcome return to the track, was runner-up in the 220 yards with a time of 24.5 secs, and both 'A' and 'B' events in the 440 yds were scooped for the Bels. by Alan Jackson, 51.8 and Dudley Gordon, 54.7 secs.

Dave Mitchell and Dudley Gordon both reached the final of the 880 where Dave was narrowly beaten by Haith of the Valley. In the mile John Thresher ran particularly well to gain third place in 4:26.0 behind Pegley and Darchambaud (S.L.H.) 4:23.0 and finish in front of Mal Robinson.

A grand total of 25 starters went to their respective marks for the 2 mile run handicap and John Leaver, a youth, emerged a popular winner by 7 seconds from Dudley Gordon who manages to find time between his continental jaunts to'get up' in these handicaps.
It is good to see Dudley Gordon in full training again after his accident early this year. The Boxing Day handicap can't be far off!

Young Blair-Fish, who joined us earlier this year, was a good winner of the race (off 3:30) with his actual time ranking 14th of the 40 runners. Chris Fairfield pulled one out of the bag for 2nd and our old friend Dudley Gordon just had to get amongst the prizes again, finishing 3rd.
Dudley Gordon Holidays offer three weeks in Carribean for £2.18s.0d.

The writer of this note has no hesitation in saying that Dudley Gordon is a handicapper's nightmare. Dudley does not win many pots in scratch competition these days (we believe it may not always have been thus).

It all ended in victory for John Thresher whose storming finish up the Chelsea Bridge slope gained him the top prize - an ultraviolet lamp suitable for the treatment of 'injuries'. Doug Maughan was second and Alan Mead, who says he is trying to mould a handicap career on that of past master Dudley Gordon, took third.
Once again Dudley Gordon reminded us that he is the uncrowned handicap king of Belgrave Harriers, this time with a clear quarter of a minute margin.
Centre left to right: Dudley Gordon, Gerry Sexton, George Piddington and Robin Brown. Bottom left to right: Simon Pritchard, Joe McDonald and Alan Painter.
Dudley Gordon, on a breezy late October Tuesday night, "did the business" on such greats as "Boofer" Bruce, Charlie Walker and Tony Stone in the twice yearly Bridges Race around Battersea Park.

Standing: John Wasbrough, Charlie Walker, Alan Lane, Rex Bale, Keith Duckett, Mark Hutton, Tony Stone, Derek Manning, Dudley Gordon. Kneeling: Paul King, Arthur Bruce, Leo Coy, Frank Barrett, Charlie Dickinson, Mike Newton, Pat Newall and Harry Porter.

…all and walker John Hall, on hand to take a few photographs, duly obliged before setting off on some Marathon training. Dudley Gordon is now gradually recovering from his knee operation. For a while he found life most difficult but is now walking again.…

Basil Walden (2) takes the 100yds title, equalling the Championship Best of 10.2, with Denis Merrett (1) 2nd in the same time and Ron Holtum (4) 3rd. Basil rejoined the Club this year and of course Dudley Gordon (7) has never ever left us.
